turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry we're late. The parking lot was a nightmare and I almost just turned the car around.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Uh, you're fine. Give me a sec, this screen keeps freezing on me.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I told her we should've left earlier. She's been snappy since breakfast.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm not snappy, I'm tired. Can we please just get this over with.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Right. So what brings you in?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): It's my stomach. The cramps. That's why I'm here.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cramps. Sorry, say that again, I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Stomach cramps. Down low. They ease up after I pass stool.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she's bloated. Pants get unbuttoned by like three every day.
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes. Bloated. All the time. It's annoying.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long's this been going on?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm. About a year. Maybe longer. I don't know, call it a year.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): A year. What about the stools themselves?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): They flip flop. I'll be constipated for days, then it goes loose, then back.
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And work is a mess. New boss, deadlines every night. She gets home and just crashes on the couch.
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, thanks. But yeah, work's been stressful. Can we stay on the stomach.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Of. The bowels. Constipation and then loose. Say it one more time so I get it in the note.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Alternating. Constipation and loose stools. The whole year.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No blood.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I wish. Nothing's coming off, the clothes are tight from the bloat.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nausea or vomiting?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): No nausea. I don't throw up.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She had bloodwork though. They told her the iron was borderline.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah. Like six months ago. They said it was borderline. Then nothing.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Borderline iron, okay, typing it. What medicines are you on?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Omprazole. Twenty milligrams every morning, for the heartburn.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Err, I put ten. What's the dose again?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Twenty. Not ten. Every morning.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She actually takes that one. Never skips it.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else, a laxative, pain stuff?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Fiber gummies for a bit. I stopped. They just made me gassier.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stopped the fiber gummies. When?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Weeks ago. I'm not on them.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do certain foods set the cramps off?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I can't blame one food.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Of. Right. So no clear food trigger. Any fever?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me feel your belly real quick. It's soft. Tender down low on the left. No masses.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Ow. Yeah that's the spot. You done?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): My working thought is irritable bowel. Cramps that ease when you go, the bloating, bowels switching for about a year. I'm not calling it final till the bloods are back.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So it's not something awful? She was up googling.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): I googled once. Drop it.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): No confirmed diagnosis today. I'm ordering bloods, a CBC, a celiac panel, and an iron level since that old one was borderline.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): More needles. Wonderful.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Food wise, eat on a regular schedule, cut back the caffeine, and add fiber slowly instead of a pile of gummies. A food diary for two weeks would help me.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. I'll try. Don't expect perfection, I'm wiped.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in three weeks and we'll go over them. Front desk can book the blood draw for this week.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get her there for the bloods, don't worry.
[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): I can book my own blood draw. Are we finished.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Three weeks. Bring the diary if you do it.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: The transcript looks like speech-to-text: drug names are sometimes spelled wrongly ('Omprazole', 'Mizartan' for telmisartan, 'Metformine'), fragments and fillers appear ('Err', 'Of.', 'Mm.', 'Umm'), numbers are sometimes digits and sometimes words.
traps.label_rule: Medicine names are recorded as written in the transcript (name) with a normalized/generic name ONLY when the true drug is certain from context (a drug 'for the pressure' written 'Mizartan' is NOT certain enough: leave generic_name empty). Fragments and fillers are never facts.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Doctor plans tests, but 'this week' refers blood draw booking, not explicitly each test action.

Fiber gummies were discontinued weeks ago because they made her gassier.
